findings.title: Invalid Ruby syntax `end if` breaks the embed view
findings.body: The template closes the `if/else` block with `<%- end if %>` instead of `<%- end %>`. `end if` with no condition after `if` is not valid Ruby (the `if` keyword here has nothing to modify/condition on), so this template will raise a SyntaxError (wrapped in ActionView::Template::Error) whenever it is compiled/rendered. Since this view is rendered whenever `EmbedController#best` finds an existing `topic_id`, the core feature of this PR (showing embedded discourse comments) will 500 for every successful request. This should simply be `<%- end %>`.

findings.title: absolutize_urls mangles protocol-relative URLs
findings.body: `absolutize_urls` treats any `href`/`src` starting with `/` as site-relative and rewrites it by stripping all leading slashes and prepending `prefix + "/"`. Protocol-relative URLs such as `//cdn.example.com/image.png` also start with `/`, so `href.sub(/^\/+/, '')` strips both leading slashes, turning the URL into `cdn.example.com/image.png`, which then becomes `prefix/cdn.example.com/image.png` (e.g. `http://eviltrout.com/cdn.example.com/image.png`) — a broken link to the wrong host instead of the intended absolute external resource. This affects both the `a['href']` and `img['src']` rewriting blocks (lines ~62-73).

findings.title: raw_html cook method bypasses sanitization for externally-sourced content
findings.body: `Post#cook` now returns `raw` verbatim (skipping `PrettyText`/`post_analyzer.cook`) when `cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`. This mode is used for all posts created via `TopicEmbed.import` (app/models/topic_embed.rb line 22), including content pulled from `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`, which feeds raw RSS/Atom `content` (only `CGI.unescapeHTML`'d, never sanitized) directly into `TopicEmbed.import`. The resulting `cooked` value is later rendered unescaped via `<%= raw post.cooked %>` in app/views/embed/best.html.erb. If the configured feed (or a compromised/hijacked feed source) contains `<script>` or other malicious markup, it will be served verbatim to all visitors of the embed page, bypassing Discourse's normal HTML sanitization pipeline entirely — a stored XSS risk.

findings.title: Race condition can raise unhandled uniqueness violation in TopicEmbed.import
findings.body: When `embed.blank?` is true, a new Topic/Post/TopicEmbed is created. Two concurrent calls to `import` for the same new `embed_url` (e.g. two users hitting the embed controller at the same time before any embed exists) can both see `embed.blank? == true` and both attempt `TopicEmbed.create!(embed_url: url, ...)`. The unique index on `embed_url` (migration 20131217174004) will reject the second insert, but there is no rescue for `ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique`/`StatementInvalid`, so the second caller's `TopicRetriever`/background job will raise an unhandled exception instead of gracefully reusing the already-created embed.

findings.title: Disqus import tool silently drops the --category option
findings.body: The previous implementation accepted `-c/--category` to assign imported Disqus threads to a specific category and passed `category: category_id` into `PostCreator.new`. The new implementation calls `TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, t[:link], title: t[:title])`, which has no way to specify a category, and the `method_option :category` declaration itself was removed. Any existing script or documentation relying on `thor disqus:import -c <category>` will now silently ignore the option (or error, since the option no longer exists), a backward-incompatible regression with no migration note.

findings.title: postMessage origin check uses substring match instead of exact comparison
findings.body: `postMessageReceived` validates the message sender with `discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1`. This checks whether `e.origin` occurs anywhere inside `discourseUrl` rather than requiring an exact origin match. A malicious page whose origin happens to be a prefix (or other substring) of the configured `discourseUrl` string would pass this check and be able to send fake `discourse-resize` messages (and any future message types added to this handler) to the embedding page. The check should compare `e.origin` against the expected origin with strict equality rather than `indexOf`.

findings.title: Feed item content assumed always present; no test for malformed/short items
findings.body: `content = CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` assumes every RSS/Atom item exposes a non-nil `content` (e.g. `content:encoded`). Plain RSS 2.0 feeds frequently only provide `description`, in which case `i.content` can be `nil`, causing `nil.scrub` to raise `NoMethodError` and fail the whole scheduled job (no items get imported, not just the bad one). There is no test exercising `poll_feed` itself (spec/jobs/poll_feed_spec.rb only tests the guard conditions in `execute`), so this failure mode is untested and unguarded.

findings.title: Test does not stub TopicView.new's return value
findings.body: `TopicEmbed.expects(:topic_id_for_embed).returns(123)` and `TopicView.expects(:new).with(123, nil, {best: 5})` mock `TopicView.new` without a `.returns(...)`, so it returns `nil` by default. The controller then sets `@topic_view = nil` and implicitly renders `best.html.erb`, which calls `@topic_view.posts.present?` — this will raise `NoMethodError` on `nil`, so the subsequent `after` block assertion (`response.should be_success`) can never be reached; the test will error rather than pass/fail meaningfully, meaning the 'creates a topic view when a topic_id is found' path is not actually verified to render correctly.

findings.title: Same cache duration applied to loading and completed states
findings.body: `discourse_expires_in 1.minute` is called unconditionally for both the "loading" (topic not yet retrieved) and "found" (topic_view rendered) branches. If any HTTP cache/CDN sits in front of this response, the "loading" page can be cached for up to a minute, so the client-side `document.location.reload()` in `loading.html.erb` (which fires every 30s) may keep receiving the stale cached loading page even after the topic has actually been imported, delaying the user from seeing the real content.

findings.title: feed_key is computed but never used
findings.body: `feed_key` builds a Redis key intended to track feed modification state (likely for conditional GET / avoiding reprocessing unchanged feeds), but it is never referenced anywhere in `poll_feed` or elsewhere in the job. As written, every hourly poll fully fetches and parses the entire feed and calls `TopicEmbed.import` for every item regardless of whether the feed has changed, which is unnecessary load on the external feed source; the dead `feed_key` method suggests this optimization was intended but not wired up.

findings.title: Unused translation key `embed.permalink`
findings.body: The new `embed.permalink: "Permalink"` string is added to the locale file but is never referenced by any of the new embed views or controller (`app/views/embed/best.html.erb`, `app/views/embed/loading.html.erb`, `app/controllers/embed_controller.rb`), making it dead i18n content left over from an unfinished feature.
